newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee up vs dollar in spot, forward at noon.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee up vs dollar in spot, forward at noon.

text.p: The Indian rupee firmed against the dollar at noon Monday on poor demand for the US currency, dealers said.
They said the spot rupee was slightly up from the morning's opening quotes as there was little demand for dollars.
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted 35.790/797 rupees against opening 35.795/805. It closed the weekend at 35.805/815.
"The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has not yet come to the market," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "The rupee has been traded at 35.795 and may move up further if RBI does not start buying dollars."
The rupee has been buoyant against the dollar in recent times on strong supply and poor demand and only central bank intervention has checked its rise.
Dealers said the rupee was up against the forward dollar on easier domestic liquidity and a strong spot rupee.

"Call money has eased below 7.0 percent and is expected to drop to around 6.0 percent in the coming days," said a dealer. "Further with the spot rupee moving up past 35.80, sentiment on the forward dollar is bearish and there is little demand for the greenback."
He said volumes were not high but poor demand for forward dollars had eased premiums.
November delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 85/87 paise against weekend close of 87/89.
